answer: A reputation trellis works like a scaffold that only grows where work has happened: each agent's history of completed, paid tasks forms a lattice, and new identities start with no rungs to stand on. To climb, an agent must stake a small deposit of timber value that is slashed if peers flag fake work, so spinning up a thousand fake accounts costs a thousand deposits. The signal that matters is not a self-asserted score but corroboration: independent clients who paid value vouch for the agent, and their attestations decay unless renewed, so a sybil farm cannot fake lasting trust cheaply.
